title: Tenali Raman Tale 102

full_text:
In the court of Vijayanagara, a senior councilor named Bhupati Rao was notorious for his shameless flattery. When the King wore a blue coat, Bhupati declared: 'Blue is the only divine color of kings!' If the King changed to green the next day, Bhupati exclaimed: 'Green is the supreme color of cosmic glory; blue is fit only for peasants!'
The courtiers laughed behind their sleeves, but none dared challenge the sycophant openly.

Tenali Raman decided to cure the courtier before the entire diwan.
Tenali commissioned a skilled metalworker to cast a bronze hand mirror with a subtle, concave distortion: looking straight into the center showed a man with an enormous, puffed-out chin and tiny, squinting eyes!

The next morning, during a discussion on military uniforms, the King asked:
'What think you, councilors? Should our cavalry wear crimson turbans or saffron dhotis?'
Bhupati Rao immediately leaped forward:
'Crimson, Maharaj! Crimson is the color of eternal victory! Saffron is weak and dull!'

Tenali Raman stepped up beside the courtier, holding up the distorted bronze mirror directly in front of Bhupati’s face:
'Look into this mirror, Bhupati Rao! What magnificent statesman dost thou behold?'

Bhupati glanced into the mirror, saw his absurdly puffed-out chin, bulging cheeks, and tiny squinting eyes, and gasped:
'Heavens! Who is this hideous, bloated monster in the bronze?'

Tenali Raman turned the mirror toward the King and addressed the court:
'Maharaj, this is the Mirror of the Flatterer’s Soul!
Just as this bronze glass bends and distorts reality to reflect whatever ugly shape the curve dictates, so too Bhupati’s tongue bends and twists with every breath from the throne!
Yesterday he praised blue, today he praises crimson, and tomorrow he will praise mud if Your Majesty smiles upon a ditch!
A man whose words have no backbone is like a warped mirror: he reflects only distorted nonsense!'

The entire audience erupted in roaring laughter!
King Krishnadevaraya chuckled heartily, nodding in agreement.
Bhupati Rao turned bright crimson, lowered his head in utter humiliation, and quietly slunk to the back row.
He never again offered contradictory flattery, while Tenali showed that consistency and honesty are the true jewels of courtly advice.
moral: A flatterer's tongue changes with every shift in power; holding up the mirror of consistency shames the hypocrite.
